B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: The official help page says connecting to an LLM is available on any plan. It does not state a separate MCP fee.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: A free Basic plan is available. The official pricing page lists Team Advantage at €30 per user per month, starting at three users and billed annually. Other current plan prices were not extracted.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: Plan, seat, or role may limit connector output; paid plans may be needed for all response data and paid features. Survey plan features and response limits vary by plan.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: The account data must be stored in the United States. LLM Connectors are unavailable for HIPAA-enabled Enterprise accounts and accounts with Enhanced Sensitive Data Protection. Team or Enterprise admins can request team-wide disablement through SurveyMonkey support.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: SurveyMonkey controls service eligibility and may apply technical or usage limits; account plan, seat, role, and organizational administration also affect access.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic:
1. Official docs divide the 20 listed operations into 12 read-only and 8 write or delete. Tool annotations (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint) are not published. [DOCS]
2. No server-enforced confirmation parameter, preview/confirm flow, or elicitation was found. Docs put review of proposed actions on the user/client. [DOCS]
3. OAuth scopes are surveys_read, surveys_write, collectors_write, responses_read, responses_read_detail, users_read. Docs say account plan, seat, or role may limit output; they do not detail role inheritance or token lifetime/revocation. Connector terms allow admin controls where configured. [OAUTH; DOCS; TERMS]
4. The help page requires US-stored account data; HIPAA-enabled Enterprise and Enhanced Sensitive Data Protection accounts are excluded. No official toolset, readonly mode, or URL filter was found. The EU endpoint was not officially confirmed. [DOCS]
5. Connector terms prohibit submitting protected health information and highly sensitive or regulated data unless the feature is designed, documented, or authorized for it. No field masking or response redaction behavior is documented. [TERMS]
6. Connector terms reserve technical, usage, and rate limits; specific MCP limits, bulk caps, truncation, and per-call charges were not found. Plan-based response limits apply to the linked product. [TERMS; PRICING HELP]
7. MCP parameter validation, type coercion, correction, and operator overrides are unknown; tool schemas were not published in accessible official sources.
8. Connector terms say the vendor may log, monitor, and audit activity for security, integrity, and compliance; actual MCP events, telemetry defaults, and opt-out are not specified. [TERMS]
9. No feedback, rating, report, or survey-feedback tool name appears in the 20 listed operations. No tool-result upsell or vendor-preference instruction was documented.
10. Official docs provide user responsibility guidance and example prompts; no server-delivered skill or behavioral instruction text was found. [DOCS]
11. No persistent agent memory or state affecting later tools/results was documented.
12. A hosted MCP endpoint is described; no hierarchy, subserver proxy, or dynamic toolsets were documented.
13. No raw API request, arbitrary SQL, script, or execute tool appears in the published list.
D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: The available evidence shows one hosted endpoint with one published flat list of operations.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: The official help page publishes 20 operations (12 read-only and 8 write/delete), without machine-readable tool identifiers or parameter schemas. The Claude connector directory lists 19 exact machine names; those 19 are included in actions.json and marked third-party because the names are confirmed there. The official page's 20th operation, “Get a statistical summary of survey responses,” is not represented as a distinct name in that directory and is not added under a guessed name. Thus actions.json contains 19 exact names, plus the official list establishes a total of 20; one official operation lacks an exact machine name. No catalogue-only actions were added. MartechDB and MCP.so showed no tool list; MCPBundles could not list tools anonymously; Pipedream's prepared page showed a loading placeholder. Agent Discoverability reports 20 tools but publishes no names in the inspected evidence.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: The official page instructs users to review granted permissions and monitor AI-proposed or completed actions. It warns that assistants may be inaccurate, incomplete, or out of date. No evidence shows the server enforces these review recommendations.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Connector terms state SurveyMonkey may log, monitor, and audit connector activity for security, integrity, and compliance. They require users not to submit data they lack authority to disclose and prohibit PHI and highly sensitive or regulated data unless expressly supported. The terms also say transmitted data may be processed by the third-party connector under its own terms after it leaves SurveyMonkey.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: The help page says the connector can create, edit, publish, search, and analyze surveys. Users can unlink the connector from Linked Accounts; admins can request team-wide disabling through support.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: OAuth discovery and the observed authentication challenge support the existence of protected access. The official tool list establishes read/write categories but no runtime annotations or confirmation enforcement. User review instructions and sensitive-data rules are documented as responsibilities/terms; no server-side enforcement mechanism was found. Logging and auditing are permitted by terms, but implementation details are not documented.

contradictions: The official help page lists 20 operations, while the Claude connector directory lists 19 exact tool names. Its list does not expose a distinct exact name for the official “Get a statistical summary of survey responses” operation; the official total is therefore one higher than the exact-name list in actions.json.

OAuth metadata exposes surveys_write and collectors_write scopes alongside read scopes, while the official help page indicates only one explicit delete operation (delete a question) among its write/delete tools; scopes indicate authorization breadth but do not map one-to-one to listed tool operations.
The help page says connector use is available on any plan, while also stating that a plan, seat, or role may limit output and that an upgrade may be required for all response data and paid features.
observations_for_research: The official documentation classifies tools in coarse read-only and write/delete groups but does not publish exact schemas, annotations, or machine identifiers.
Access is connected to account data region and enterprise security configuration, as well as plan, seat, and role limits.
Connector terms explicitly assign responsibility for evaluating AI outputs and actions to the customer and authorize possible vendor logging, monitoring, and auditing.
